title: What the ledger claims — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
What the ledger claims — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the address. 8 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 3 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 5 pair(s); the theorems fall into 4 strand(s), the largest of 3. Most binding: rounds (3), saving (2), addr4 (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: merkle.lean. Built on it: speed.lean. Checking this cluster needs 4 file(s): src/proof/ledgerclaims.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/merkle.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to ca6ad553-fa5e-854d-8d19-3c2829bfe6cd. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 8, 0, 6, 7, 1, 2). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: reach.lean (3 observed, 0.44 expected, lift 6.76), address.lean (4 observed, 1.51 expected, lift 2.65), energy.lean (3 observed, 1.86 expected, lift 1.61). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 14.79; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.61. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 1.5% of them — above chance by this measure, though with 33 clusters about two are expected there by chance alone.

Prior art. `membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling` and `membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear` restate the O(log n) membership proof of a hash tree — Ralph Merkle, 1979 (thesis); CRYPTO 1987 — which merkle.lean in this same deposit already credits. Classified `unbounded` on the ground that the subject is this deposit's own ledger; the ledger is its own, the logarithm is not. Bounded: what is not prior art is what THIS ledger claims — the 967-receipt case, the saving arithmetic, and the 128-bit seal width as this deposit mints it. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. a_seal_is_128_bits — (toUuidBytes [97]).length * 8 = 128 record
  2. membership_grows_by_one_seal_per_doubling — rounds 40 2 = 1 ∧ rounds 40 4 = 2 ∧ rounds 40 8 = 3 ∧ rounds 40 16 = 4 ∧ rounds 40 32 = 5 ∧ rounds 40 64 = 6 ∧ rounds 40 128 = 7 ∧ rounds 40 256 = 8 record
  3. membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear — rounds 40 1024 = 10 ∧ rounds 40 1024 < 1024 ∧ rounds 40 1024 * 128 < 1024 * 128 record
  4. the_967_receipt_case — saving 967 20 = 947 ∧ 20 + 947 = 967 record
  5. a_saving_never_exceeds_its_value — (List.range 40).all (fun v => (List.range 40).all (fun w => saving v w ≤ v)) record
  6. more_payloads_than_addresses_must_collide — ((List.range 17).map addr4).eraseDups.length < 17 record
  7. the_address_does_not_determine_the_payload — ((List.range 17).any (fun a => (List.range 17).any (fun b => a != b && addr4 a == addr4 b))) = true record
  8. a_proof_is_smaller_than_its_set_across_the_octave — (List.range' 2 255).all (fun n => rounds 40 n < n) record
